newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Montenegro bourse September turnover sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Montenegro bourse September turnover sharply up.

text.p: The Montenegro Stock Exchange on Friday reported a sharp 53 percent surge in its turnover during September, despite tightened liquidity.
The total turnover in September jumped to 49.6 million dinars ($9.8 million) in 148 transactions, up on 32.5 million dinars in August," the bourse said in its report.
The central bank's decision to introduce a 10 percent reserve requirement weighed on the market activity, Dejan Vasovic of the Montenegro bourse said.
"National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) reserve requirement tightened market liquidity, which in turn caused greater thirst for fresh borrowing," Vasovic told Reuters.
According to the bourse report, short-term securities, mainly the NBY short-term bonds, generated nearly 62 percent of the total turnover.

Giro money market segment -- trading surplus liquidity among banks -- accounted for another 38 percent or 18.84 million dinars, the bourse said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
